title: The Black Sheep and the White Stallion (ES)
summary: A foreign nobleman refuses to walk near dark-skinned peasants, boasting of his fair complexion. Birbal uses black and white animals to dismantle racial vanity. [ES]
full_text:
A haughty nobleman from the northern mountains named Mirza Rustam arrived in Agra. Having very pale skin, he looked down with open disgust upon the sun-browned peasants and dark-skinned laborers of Hindustan, refusing to let them touch his carriage or walk upon his shadow.

During a state durbar, the nobleman arrogantly remarked to Emperor Akbar: 'Your Majesty, it is a pity that so many of your subjects possess dark, sunburnt skin. White is the color of purity, light, and nobility; black is the color of darkness, night, and low birth!'

Akbar was offended by the insult to his people, but Birbal stepped forward with a serene, polite smile:

'Mirza Sahib, your admiration of colors is fascinating. Let us examine how your theory operates in the imperial stables.'

Birbal led the court to the imperial stables and pastures.

In the first paddock stood an extraordinarily beautiful, pure white Arabian stallion, with a silken white mane and glowing coat.

In the second paddock stood a flock of hardy, black mountain sheep from the Himalayas, covered in thick, curly jet-black wool.

Birbal turned to the pale nobleman:

'Mirza Sahib, look at this white stallion. Its coat is as white as freshly fallen snow. Yet look at the floor of its stall: when it drops its waste, what color is it?'

'It is brown and dark,' the nobleman replied, puzzled.

Birbal continued: 'And when winter arrives in the freezing mountain passes, can you shear the white stallion's fur to weave a warm blanket to save a freezing child's life?'

'No,' the nobleman admitted. 'A horse's coat cannot be spun into wool.'

Birbal walked to the black sheep, stroked their dark wool, and said:

'Now look at these black sheep. Their wool is as black as midnight. Yet from this black wool, our weavers spin warm, soft blankets and coats that preserve the lives of thousands of soldiers and children during the bitter Himalayan winters!

'And from these black sheep, the shepherds milk sweet, nourishing white milk that feeds newborn infants!

'So tell me, Mirza Sahib: which is more noble? The white stallion whose coat cannot warm a child, or the black sheep whose dark wool protects life and whose milk is pure white nourishment?

'Nature teaches us that color is merely an outer garment dyed by sun and climate. The true nobility of a human being resides in the warmth of his heart and the service of his hands!'

The pale nobleman hung his head in burning shame, while the entire assembly cheered. Akbar embraced Birbal for defending the dignity of all human beings with peerless eloquence.
